sentenceSets.sentence: The tumid prose style of the report communicated effort without communicating substance.

answerChoices.reasoning: Verbose (using more words than necessary) shares excessive wordiness but focuses on length rather than the swollen, inflated quality the sentence associates with empty effort.
Grandiose (impressively large or ambitious) shares exaggeration but emphasizes grand scale rather than swollen emptiness.
Ornate (elaborately decorated) involves excessive style but does not capture the swollen, bloated quality of tumid prose.
Pretentious (claiming more importance than warranted) is close but emphasizes false claims rather than the swollen, inflated form of expression.
Complicated (complex and difficult) might result from tumid style but is not its defining characteristic.
Obscure (unclear or hard to understand) might accompany tumid prose but refers to clarity rather than stylistic inflation.
Pompous (excessively dignified) overlaps with inflated self-importance but is about manner rather than the swollen quality of style.
Clear (easy to understand) is opposite to prose that communicates poorly despite apparent effort.
Concise (brief and precise) is opposite to the swollen, inflated wordiness of tumid style.
Sparse (thinly distributed or scant) is opposite to the swelling and inflation.
Direct (straightforward and unambiguous) is opposite to the obfuscating effect of tumid prose.

sentenceSets.sentence: His tumid cheeks from the dental procedure made him look older than his years, an unexpected side effect of the anesthesia.

answerChoices.reasoning: Puffy (swollen from fluid) is very close to tumid in describing swelling, but the medical context of dental work makes tumid more precisely descriptive of post-procedure inflammation.
Bloated (swollen from excess) shares the swelling quality but often implies distension from internal pressure, less specific to the localized post-dental swelling.
Enlarged (made bigger) describes the size change but lacks the specific quality of swelling from inflammation.
Distended (stretched out) emphasizes the spreading quality but is less commonly used for facial swelling than tumid.
Numb (unable to feel sensation) is a symptom of anesthesia mentioned in the sentence but not a description of physical appearance.
Discolored (altered in color) might accompany swelling but is not itself a description of puffiness.
Bruised (marked by impact injury) can occur after dental work but does not specifically describe the swollen appearance.
Gaunt (thin and hollow-cheeked) is the opposite of swollen cheeks.
Sunken (depressed inward) is opposite to the outward swelling described.
Hollow (empty inside or sunken) is opposite to the fullness of swelling.
Angular (having sharp angles or edges) is opposite to the rounded, swollen appearance of tumid cheeks.

sentenceSets.sentence: The speaker's tumid language and breathless delivery suggested passion, but the audience sensed only desperation beneath the theatrical presentation.

answerChoices.reasoning: Effusive (expressing feeling with unrestrained enthusiasm) shares the excess but emphasizes emotional overflow rather than swollen, inflated expression.
Florid (flowery and ornate) overlaps with excessive stylistic inflation but focuses on decoration rather than swollen, bloated quality.
Bombastic (high-sounding but with little meaning) is very close but emphasizes hollow grandiosity rather than the swollen, inflated form.
Overwrought (elaborated excessively) shares excess but focuses on complexity rather than the swollen, bloated quality.
Exuberant (enthusiastically energetic) involves excess energy but is not necessarily false or swollen in expression.
Emphatic (expressed with force or conviction) involves strong delivery but not necessarily the swollen, inflated quality.
Theatrical (exaggerated for dramatic effect) shares artificiality but is mentioned as a separate quality in the sentence.
Understated (presented as less important than it is) is opposite to the swollen, inflated expression.
Restrained (controlled and moderate) is opposite to the bloated, excessive language.
Subdued (quiet and lacking force) is contrary to the exaggerated, swollen delivery described.
Muted (softened or dampened) opposes the loud, swollen presentation.
